compensating.why: hop 1 asks for an event only when the series has more than one item
hop 2 returns early for an empty data list
hop 3 counts the maximum age inclusively (one more period)

ownership_reason: Only the gold decides whether any item of the series is aged and whether a SeriesChangeEvent is sent; hops 1-4 pass the series, its data list, the maximum age and the notify flag along unchanged. On the trigger input (two items, timespan 2, maximum age 2, notify true) nothing is aged and the series does not change, yet the gold sends a SeriesChangeEvent, which reports a change. The convention that the event is sent only when items were removed is pinned outside the gold: the facade's own javadoc ('a SeriesChangeEvent is sent to registered listeners IF any items are removed'); Series.fireSeriesChanged ('signalling to registered listeners that the series has been changed'); the sibling overload TimeSeries.removeAgedItems(long, boolean) ('if (removed && notify)'), with TimeSeriesTests testRemoveAgedItems2 asserting no event after a call that removes nothing; TimeSeries.delete(RegularTimePeriod), which sends the event only when the period exists, with TimeSeriesTests testDelete2 asserting no event after deleting an absent period; TimeSeries.clear, which sends it only for a non-empty series. No one-line change of the values passed above the gold restores the behaviour: the gold notifies whenever it is asked to and the series has two or more items, and the trigger needs an event on [1999, 2001] with maximum age 1 and none with maximum age 2.
